https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-hits-targe.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5I9h4 Ukraine is taking the war 'back to where it came from' with drone strikes deep inside Russia, said President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Sunday Image: REUTERS Advertisement Ukrainian drones rained down on numerous military, energy and civilian infrastructure sites deep inside Russia on Sunday, killing at least eight people overnight. Russia's Defense Ministry said its forces downed 635 drones over the course of the attacks. Two people were killed in the city of Engels on the Volga River when drones hit residential buildings. Another apartment complex in nearby Saratov City was also damaged. Three people were reported killed and two injured in the Udmurtia region (1,300 kilometers from Ukraine ), and another three killed and five injured in Belgorod according to local officials. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Sunday said Kyiv had targeted an oil refinery in Saratov and a military base that is home to Russian long-range bombers in Engels. Zelenskyy said the attacks were his country's answer to Russian aggression and thanked Ukrainian forces for taking the war "back to where it came from." Kyiv said fires had damaged both sites and that its forces had also struck an oil depot in the western Kaluga region. Unverified video uploaded to social media sites purported to show fires burning at the Saratov oil facility. Why is Ukraine targeting Wildberries warehouses? Ukraine again targeted the online retailer Wildberries in its attacks, striking a logistics warehouse in Samara — more than 800 kilometers (500 miles) from Ukraine's front-line positions. Sunday's attacks on Wildberries were just the latest onslaught on the retail giant , which Kyiv says aids Russia's military. Kyiv has attacked nearly a dozen Wildberries warehouses since July 18. No casualties were reported at the facility and local management said that a fire at the site had been brought under control. Although the number of drones that Russia claims to have downed cannot be confirmed, the figure is indicative of the scale of Kyiv's effort to strike Russia deep inside its own territory as it defends itself against an army that launched a full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022. The Wildberries attacks are seen as an attempt to bring President Vladimir Putin 's war home to Russia's citizens, applying pressure to the country's already anaemic economy in hopes of finally ending Moscow's ongoing invasion . https://www.politico.eu/article/germany-.text: BERLIN — The German government expects it will need almost €12 billion to build a new arsenal of long-range weapons aimed at deterring Russia, according to defense ministry documents seen by POLITICO. The weapons would give German forces the ability to hit targets hundreds or even thousands of kilometers behind the front — potentially including command centers, airfields, missile launchers and supply hubs. Internal documents call the effort a top priority for both Germany and NATO — coming at a time when European countries are rearming to deter what they see as a rising threat from Russia. Advertisement Advertisement They say the goal is to allow German forces to strike “far into the rear area of an adversary” and maintain the ability to respond with conventional weapons “below the nuclear threshold.” The plan has four parts, with the first weapons due as early as next year and the most advanced systems built jointly with the U.K. and planned for the middle of the next decade. Internal ministry talking points say “almost €12 billion” in budget funds are expected to be needed for the buildup. The money has not yet been approved. Another ministry document says the costs have been estimated and submitted as part of the government’s budget planning process. Germany’s defense ministry declined to comment on the figure or individual programs. “The measures you refer to are generally subject to the approval of the German Bundestag,” a ministry spokesperson told POLITICO. The ministry can only comment after parliament considers them, the spokesperson added. Advertisement Advertisement Missiles as soon as next year The fastest part of the plan is a new low-cost cruise missile that Germany wants to start fielding in 2027. POLITICO reported in June that the defense ministry was looking at missiles from U.S.-Israeli startup Covenant Industries and Ukrainian-linked companies as it searched for weapons that could be bought in large numbers and put into service quickly. The new documents show the effort has progressed. They name three candidates: Covenant’s Anthem missile, the BARS missile offered by an unnamed Ukrainian company, and the Flamingo from Ukrainian company Fire Point. Germany is in contract talks with two of those suppliers, with the aim of receiving missiles for qualification by next year. Berlin is already preparing framework contracts for later mass production. The documents describe the low-cost missile as a “cost-efficient and, above all, mass-producible” weapon that can be used alongside much more expensive missiles. Advertisement Advertisement That follows a lesson Berlin says it has drawn from the war in Ukraine, where Kyiv is having increasing success using drones and missiles to hit Russian military infrastructure and refineries. When POLITICO first reported on the low-cost missile program in June, the defense ministry said hitting important targets far behind enemy lines had become “indispensable for credible deterrence.” “Cost-effective systems can overwhelm enemy air defenses through mass attacks and are therefore of high operational value,” the ministry said at the time. Filling the Tomahawk gap The next part of the plan is American. Chancellor Friedrich Merz told the Bundestag in early July that Germany had reached an agreement with the U.S. government during the NATO summit in Ankara to acquire American Tomahawk cruise missiles and deploy them in Germany. “We are closing an important strategic gap in our defense,” Merz said, adding that Germany would develop its own European systems at the same time. Advertisement Advertisement Germany’s internal target, according to the documents, is to have an initial capability of U.S. Typhon launchers armed with Tomahawk missiles by the end of the decade. The purchase would give Berlin a proven long-range weapon while European alternatives are being developed. The final two parts of the plan are being developed with Britain. Germany and the U.K. are working on a new high-end cruise missile and a hypersonic glide weapon, part of last year’s Trinity House Agreement, with the documents showing the goal of an initial capability by the middle of the next decade. The two governments have already said publicly that their new long-range weapons should be able to reach targets more than 2,000 kilometers away. That project accounts for most of the money in Germany’s current estimate. Advertisement Advertisement One internal document puts nearly €9 billion toward development and procurement of the weapons, plus €182 million for keeping them in service. It lists another €1.8 billion for cruise missile development and procurement and €97 million for maintenance. Those figures add up to around €11 billion. Separate ministry talking points put the overall expected required funding at “almost €12 billion.” For Germany, the missile plan marks a major change. Instead of waiting for one new European missile, Berlin wants several types of weapons: cheaper missiles that can be produced in large numbers, American Tomahawks available sooner, and more advanced European weapons later. The buildup is taking place as German military leaders warn that Russia could be able to attack NATO territory by the end of the decade. Berlin wants to make sure that if deterrence fails, Russian military infrastructure would not be safe simply because of its distance from the front lines. Advertisement

http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/30/passe.text: Seven people have reportedly died after a passenger ship capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus on Sunday.The vessel, which was reportedly sailing from Kyreneia in Cyprus to the Turkish port of Taşucu, sank at around midday.Turkey's Interior Ministry said 259 passengers and eight crew members were on board the vessel when it began taking on water roughly 6 km off the coast of Kyreneia.Murat Senkul, the mayor of Kyreneia, described the situation as "very serious" in a post on Facebook, adding that a rescue operation was under way.Speaking to CNN Turk, Tufan Erhürman, the president of the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, said: "So far, we have reached 244 people. Seven of those reached have lost their lives, and 23 people are missing."Video footage circulating on social media appears to show passengers in life jackets sitting on the overturned ship as they wait to be reached.The cause of the incident is not yet clear.Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides' office said in statement on the sinking: “Our position is clear: when human lives are at risk, we contribute with every available means.""The Republic of Cyprus has the resources, the operational capacity, and, above all, the readiness to provide immediate assistance," it added.Cyprus has been divided since 1974, when a Greek-backed military coup led to an invasion by Turkish forces and the division of the island.This is a developing story. Check back for further details.

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/clyl.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Family members and other officials came to receive the coffin at Entebbe airport By Wycliffe Muia Published 4 September 2026, 11:54 BST Updated 2 hours ago The body of a popular traditional ruler who was the world's youngest reigning monarch has been flown home to Uganda where President Yoweri Musveni was amongst the mourners gathered at Entebbe airport to pay their respects. King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV died in the US last week aged 34 after receiving treatment for an aggressive form of cancer . The Tooro king will be buried next Saturday - the day he had hoped to celebrate the anniversary of his coronation. He had ascended the throne aged just three and was crowned when he turned 18. The return of his body marks the start of the Tooro kingdom's official nine-day mourning period amid a growing dispute over who should succeed him. Image source, Reuters Image caption, There was a sombre mood as the police escorted the coffin from the plane Uganda is governed by an elected president and parliament, but it has several traditional kingdoms that continue to have significant cultural influence despite not having political power. Oyo, who Guinness World Records listed as the world's youngest reigning monarch , external , ruled over more than two million people. He was the 13th monarch of a kingdom that was founded in the early 19th Century. After a brief ceremony at the airport, his body was flown by military helicopter to Kyegegwa in western Uganda, where the Tooro Kingdom is located, before being taken by road to the royal palace in Fort Portal. It will lie in state at Karuziika Palace for the mourning period and members of the public will be allowed to pay their respects and prayers will be held there each evening. On Thursday, Uganda's parliament held a special tribute to King Oyo, with MPs remembering him as a modernising monarch who championed education, health and opportunities for young people. Image source, Uganda government Image caption, President Yoweri Museveni laid a wreath on King Oyo's coffin Image source, Uganda Media Centre Image caption, Royal mourners watched on during the short ceremony at the airport Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja described him as a "symbol of unity" and praised his work raising awareness about HIV and Aids among young people. Opposition MPs also paid tribute, with acting opposition leader Patrick Nsamba Oshabe saying: "Heritage and development were never rivals in his hands." President Museveni has ordered an official burial for the monarch and national flags will fly at half-mast for three days around the funeral. On Wednesday, the Tooro kingdom's Prime Minister, Calvin Armstrong Rwomiire Akiiki, said the king had asked officials not to disclose the seriousness of his illness because he believed he would recover and return to his people. He said the monarch had hoped to return home for this year's Empango - the annual celebration of his coronation - on 12 September. "He was confident in his recovery," Akiiki said. His death has triggered uncertainty over the future of the monarchy as Oyo was not officially married. But Akiiki has said the king had a young son, whose identity would be revealed later in accordance with Tooro customs. President Museveni also said the king's mother, Queen Best Kemigisa, had told him that her son had left an heir. But Charles Kamurasi, who is head of the Babiito royal clan from which Tooro's kings are chosen, said he knew nothing about the reported child, prompting an unusual public disagreement among senior figures in the kingdom. Others within the royal clan have questioned why they were apparently unaware of the child. "The prime minister is not supposed to talk about the king's heir. It is a cultural process," one royal clan member was quoted as saying by Uganda's state-owned New Vision newspaper. "How can we, blood relatives, not know of the child, and the prime minister says he knows? That is totally out of order," the clan member added. Akiiki has since appealed for the dispute to be dealt with privately, saying he wanted to meet other elders to resolve their differences. "Words spoken in moments of grief can deepen divisions that may take years to repair," he warned. Image source, Reuters Image caption, The casket with the body of the king was then flown by military helicopter to western Uganda Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, King Oyo ascended to the throne at the age of three - and was then crowned on reaching adulthood at 18 in 2010 The Ugandan government has also intervened, urging people not to spread speculation about the succession on social media. Culture Minister Henry Tumukunde said Ugandans should rely on official information from the government and the Tooro Kingdom, adding that any dispute would be dealt with under law governing traditional and cultural leaders. "The whole world is watching how Uganda mourns its king," he said, urging people to show "restraint and respect". The Tooro Kingdom follows a hereditary system in selecting its monarch. King Oyo ascended the throne in 1995 and became an international curiosity because of his young age. Before his burial, a church funeral service will be held at a local church. His body will then be carried in a traditional procession to the Karambi Royal Tombs, with burial is expected to be completed by 14:00 local time. According to Tooro tradition, kings are not buried in the evening.
